events.title: Traditional Date of Pompeii's Destruction (Disputed)
events.description: Long-held tradition dates the eruption of Mount Vesuvius, which buried Pompeii and Herculaneum, to August 24-25, 79 CE, based on Pliny the Younger's account. Archaeological evidence such as autumn fruits and a charcoal inscription suggests the eruption may have occurred later, in October or November.
events.significance: The eruption preserved Roman cities in remarkable detail, giving historians and archaeologists an unparalleled window into everyday life in the ancient world.

events.title: Galileo Demonstrates His Telescope in Venice
events.description: Galileo Galilei presented his improved telescope, with about 8x to 9x magnification, to the Venetian Senate from the bell tower of St. Mark's, showing its value for spotting ships at sea.
events.significance: The demonstration led to Galileo's own astronomical observations, which supported the Copernican model and helped transform modern astronomy.

events.title: Liberation of Paris
events.description: German General Dietrich von Choltitz surrendered Paris to Allied forces, with the French 2nd Armored Division under General Leclerc and the Resistance playing leading roles. Choltitz disregarded Hitler's orders to destroy the city.
events.significance: The liberation ended four years of Nazi occupation and was a major morale and strategic victory for the Allies in World War II.

events.title: Linus Torvalds Announces Linux
events.description: Finnish student Linus Torvalds posted a message to a Usenet newsgroup announcing he was working on a free operating system kernel as a hobby, which became Linux.
events.significance: Linux grew into one of the most influential pieces of software in history, powering most servers, Android devices, and supercomputers worldwide, and became a cornerstone of open-source software.

events.title: Voyager 1 Enters Interstellar Space
events.description: NASA's Voyager 1 probe, launched in 1977, crossed the heliopause into interstellar space, as later confirmed by data analysis on plasma density changes.
events.significance: Voyager 1 became the first human-made object to leave the heliosphere and enter the space between the stars.
